content: Selenium sulfide is a topical antiseborrheic and antifungal agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of tinea versicolor, seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp, and dandruff. It is not intended for systemic use and should only be applied externally. For the treatment of dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, the recommended regimen involves applying the product twice weekly for two weeks. After achieving control, the frequency of application can be reduced to weekly, biweekly, or even every three to four weeks, depending on the individual’s needs. Overuse should be avoided, as the product should only be applied as frequently as necessary to maintain control. For the treatment of tinea versicolor, the product should be applied to the affected areas, lathered with a small amount of water, and left on the skin for 10 minutes before rinsing thoroughly. This process should be repeated once daily for seven consecutive days. Selenium sulfide is contraindicated in individuals with known hypersensitivity to any of its components. It should not be applied to broken or inflamed skin, as this may increase absorption and lead to adverse effects. If an allergic reaction occurs, use should be discontinued immediately. Care should also be taken to avoid contact with the eyes or genital area, as this may cause irritation or burning. Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include skin irritation, occasional increased hair loss, and discoloration of hair, which can be minimized by thorough rinsing after use. Some individuals may also experience oiliness or dryness of the hair and scalp. Postmarketing data on adverse reactions is limited. Selenium sulfide is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA when used for the treatment of tinea versicolor. There are no animal reproduction studies or data on its effects on human fetal development or reproductive capacity. As a precaution, it is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women for this indication. There is also no specific guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. The mechanism of action of selenium sulfide involves a cytostatic effect on epidermal and follicular epithelial cells, reducing the production of corneocytes. It is available as a 2.5% topical suspension and should be stored at controlled room temperature (20°-25°C or 68°-77°F). The product should be shaken well before use and kept tightly capped. Jewelry should be removed prior to application, as the product may cause damage to metal. For dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, the application involves massaging 1-2 teaspoons of the suspension into a wet scalp, allowing it to remain for 2-3 minutes, rinsing thoroughly, and repeating the process. For tinea versicolor, the suspension should be applied to the affected areas, lathered with water, left on for 10 minutes, and rinsed thoroughly. Hands should be washed thoroughly after application. Patients should be counseled on the potential for skin irritation or sensitization and advised to discontinue use if sensitivity reactions occur. Contact with mucous membranes, particularly in the eyes, should be avoided. When applied to the body for tinea versicolor, irritation may occur in sensitive areas such as skin folds or the genital region, and these areas should be rinsed thoroughly after application. Selenium sulfide is marketed under brand names such as Dandrex®, Selsun Blue Medicated Treatment®, Selseb®, Selenos®, and Tersi Foam®. There is no established interaction between selenium sulfide and alcohol, but patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol use while using this medication.
